newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts gain with cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts gain with cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Monday in a lackluster session, with front months lifted by a firmer physical market though prices were still stuck in recent technical ranges, industry sources said.
May climbed two cents to close at $1.953 per million British thermal units. June settled 0.1 cent higher at $1.996. Other deferreds ended mixed, with 1999 contracts losing ground.

"I'd be more surprised to see us break $1.85 (in May) than $2. If there is a break, I think it will be to the upside, but I don't see it happening this week," said one Texas trader, adding it would take better cooling load to drive prices up.

Despite stepped up injections likely in the second half of the month and forecasts for cooler midweek weather, few expected a significant rally, with stocks comfortable and little cooling or heating demand on the near-term horizon.
"There was an opportunity last week to move up on the (cold) weather and it didn't materialize. Things will really have to change for us to move up," the Texas trader said.
Technical traders agreed the market was range-bound, with May trendline support at $1.88 and more buying likely at $1.85 and $1.825. Resistance was seen at $1.975, $1.99, $2.05 and $2.095.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices were talked up slightly Monday to the mid-to-high $1.90s. Midcontinent pipes gained a similar amount to the mid-to-high $1.80s. New York city gate gas was talked on either side of $2.40, also up modestly.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip rose 0.9 cent to $2.143 NYMEX said 24,070 Hub contracts traded, up slightly from Friday's revised tally of 23,579.
No Permian or Alberta natgas contracts traded Friday.

On KCBT, May finished 2.1 cents higher at $1.82, while deferreds ended up by 0.4 to one cent. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.1 cent to 13.3 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 153 lots changed hands, up from Friday's total of 96.
